title: How to make gatherable resource s more evident ?

posts.author: Jeenah
posts.body:
Hello there boyos ! Yes, yes, i'm still alive. Took a little smash on the break pedal for my project before the burnout.
So ... I'm actually searching for ways to make gatherable resources on the maps more evident for the player. In a cave i set-up, some crystals can be gathered, and they shine. But i can't put a shining effect on wood, it would be stoopid (Or even fore bones).
Do you have any idea on how to make the harvestable easier to spot ? (Because in the game i'm doing, the player will require some materials that can only be harvested to craft some very important gear/strong armors for his companions).
#DragonBone Armor for his Dragon ... "friend"

That's what pretty much every game I've seen that does something like this has.
The typical indicator is a little twinkle over the item; alternatively, to see an exclamation mark or something.
There are a number of plugins for this, such as:
MZ Action Indicators
FEATURES Enables you to display an icon above the event the player is facing. This icon has a floating up and down movement and is determined using a tag inside a comment anywhere on an event’s act…
galvs-scripts.com
The only other things I've seen are highlighting the entire graphic of the item, or having a minimap with icons on it representing the presence of resources.

posts.body: Also, if you have a clear handle on yo palette, you can make harvestable stuff a certain colour? Not helpful for colourblind peeps, but somethin' to consider?

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Sparkles, signage, and some-cool-popup are the main ways I usually see.
I prefer sparkles, but it doesn't have to be actual sparkles in your game. The point is to draw your player's eyes to the object so that they'll be more likely to interact with it. For plants it could be bugs flying around it or the flowers/fruit moving slightly, for trees it could be ant trails, a woodpecker tapping on the tree, even sap oozing from a gash in the tree.
Just make sure that early in the game you teach your players that things that have 'sparkles' like that should be interacted with.

posts.author: kirbwarrior
posts.body:
There's various ways to draw in someone's eyes, but it's very important that you pick something you're not using already with your map design.
SIgnificant palette change. Contrasting colors, hard borders, brights colors on dark backgrounds, these all stick out pretty hard. This is great for resources that gather in a place of similar objects such as usable wood in a forest, useful bugs in a field, etc.
Make it look "wrong", such as using a different artstyle or having something clash about how the resource sits on the map. This is good for resources that are otherworldly or blatantly important such as special metals, alien materials, meteorites, etc.
A meta object that is essentially a mini-HUD. Sparkles are common, but I've also seen exclamation marks, arrows, little radar circles, etc. To help make it simultaneously stick out more and be less obtrusive, make this a HUD option that you can de/activate with a button press (such as Q since that isn't doing much on maps) and things like arrows are very obvious to the player (for example, FF7 has a hand icon over the player and arrows over exists that can be turned off with Select).
Moving/shaking objects immediately jump out on a static map. Setting an object to Stepping gives it simple movement.
You can look at NPCs and see a lot of this. NPCs don't look like terrain, they are often moving in some way, and they tend to have clashing colors compared to more muted differences with tilesets.
